informed_by.finding: Phase 3A showed a consistent upward token-Markov-minus-trigram trajectory from K=1 to K=4, while only about 36%–48% of validation tokens were affected at N=64.
informed_by.status: post-hoc exploratory follow-up, not Level-2 retrofit

mechanism.important_control: Across N=64,256,1024, K=4, code alphabet size=16, code length=4, fallback mapping, master codebook, and occurrence-level variant choice are held fixed. Only the number of active TRAIN-selected lexical families changes.
mechanism.master_key_policy: Fit one 1024-word master codebook per source/seed from CONTROL TRAIN; N=64 and N=256 activate prefixes of the same frequency-ranked master target list, so mappings and variant choices for shared words are identical across N.
mechanism.name: related_multi_code_nomenclator_coverage
mechanism.phase3a_comparison_note: Phase 3A used two-glyph target codes; Phase 3A.2 uses four-glyph target codes in every condition. Therefore Phase-3A.2 N=64 is an internal baseline and is not treated as numerically identical to the Phase-3A N=64/K=4 condition.

primary_prediction: Holding K=4 and code geometry fixed, increasing active lexical coverage from N=64 to N=256 to N=1024 should move the token-Markov-minus-matched-trigram validation delta upward (less negative and potentially positive), while the other four Voynich-direction relations remain positive.
question: With related surface variation held fixed at K=4, does increasing the fraction of lexical items receiving variable ciphertext forms continue to weaken exact-token sequential predictability toward the Voynich regime while preserving the other four predictive relations?
